paragraphs: Adient plc ("Adient") is a global leader in the automotive seating supply industry with leading market positions in the Americas, Europe and Asia and maintains longstanding relationships with the largest global automotive original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"). Adient's proprietary technologies extend into virtually every area of automotive seating solutions, including complete seating systems, frames, mechanisms, foam, head restraints, armrests and trim covers. Adient is a global seat supplier with the capability to design, develop, engineer, manufacture, and deliver complete seat systems and components in every major automotive producing region in the world.

Adient designs, manufactures and markets a full range of seating systems and components for passenger cars, commercial vehicles and light trucks, including vans, pick-up trucks and sport/crossover utility vehicles. Adient operates approximately 200 wholly- and majority-owned manufacturing, assembly or sequencing facilities, with operations in 29 countries. Additionally, Adient has partially-owned affiliates in China, Asia, Europe and North America. Through its global footprint and vertical integration, Adient leverages its capabilities to drive growth in the automotive seating industry.

Adient's business model is focused on developing and maintaining long-term customer relationships, which allows Adient to successfully grow with leading global OEMs. Adient and its engineers work closely with customers as vehicle platforms are developed, which results in close ties with key decision makers at OEM customers.

Global Manufacturing Footprint Adient is a global leader in automotive seating. With more than 65,000 employees operating in approximately 200 manufacturing, assembly or sequencing facilities in 29 countries worldwide, Adient produces and delivers automotive seating for all vehicle classes and all major OEMs. From complete seating systems to individual components, Adient's manufacturing capabilities span every aspect of the automotive seat-making process. Integrated, in-house skills allows Adient to take products from research and design all the way to engineering and manufacturing and into millions of vehicles every year.

Operational Efficiencies Adient intends to maintain high capacity utilization and increase its efficiency through continued use of standardized manufacturing processes, which represent a core competency. These standardized manufacturing processes allow Adient to deliver high quality levels and minimize waste. Adient achieves scale advantages through a global manufacturing footprint and an integrated supply chain. Adient also creates efficiencies and optimizes inventory, reduces freight and direct labor costs through its integrated modular assembly process. Adient fosters an environment of continuous improvement and identifies best business practices through the analysis of process and cost metrics, which are then shared globally throughout Adient's manufacturing network.

To ensure appropriate service levels, minimal inventory and optimal factory utilization, Adient employs a Sales & Operational Planning, or S&OP, process. A well-executed S&OP process provides two strategic advantages: focused customer service and on-time delivery which result in both customer retention and the opportunity for market share gain.

Investing in Technology Adient continues to invest in technology and innovation by utilizing automation in metals, foam, trim and complete seat operations as well as expanding the use of artificial intelligence ("AI"). AI technology is being pursued to reduce direct labor costs, improve accuracy and to ensure repeatable and reproducible results.

Longstanding Customer Relationships with Leading Global OEMs Adient works with OEMs to develop complete seating solutions to meet consumer expectations for performance, safety and comfort. Adient does business with all major global OEM customers, and in many cases, works closely with those customers to develop a seating solution integrated into the overall vehicle appearance and architecture.

Through dedicated customer teams, Adient maintains close relationships with its global OEM customers. These relationships enable Adient to clearly understand its customers' needs so that it is positioned to meet its customers' requirements. Adient's customer teams also lead the new business acquisition process, which ensures alignment with Adient's product, process and manufacturing strategies.

Product Innovation and Process Leadership Adient has a strong record for developing winning product and process technologies over many years, which has created a competitive advantage for Adient and its customers. Management expects to increase investment in innovation.

Adient utilizes a global Core Product Portfolio, or CPP, strategy for part and design reuse in all of its product applications. Adient intends to continue investing in its CPP to sustain and expand its market success and to leverage its existing modular and scalable systems and interchangeable components. Through the CPP strategy, Adient provides high quality products for its customers with market competitive cost and mass (low weight to improve fuel economy) while meeting their performance requirements. Adient continues to use its CPP to advance Adient's lean manufacturing initiatives by providing standard, flexible processes that reduce complexity, inventory and floor space. This will yield reductions in development time, product cost and investment.

Global Development Network Adient participates in innovating and developing key competitive differentiators in the automotive seating business. In the development process, key downstream elements of the product are locked in, including material costs, plant conversion costs, quality characteristics and certain technical requirements. Adient uses a common product development process globally that ensures that these elements are correct at the outset of the development process, reflects the best practices of Adient's operations worldwide and meets the expectations of Adient's diverse customer base. Its product launch system is customizable and scalable based on customer and product requirements.

Adient's worldwide engineering network includes ten core development centers. These development centers utilize a globally consistent approach to the process for developing seating products. By leveraging a network of subject matter technical experts, Adient efficiently implements best practices and improves product cost and quality. Adient's product development practices also entail leveraging low cost country development centers in India, China, Czech Republic, Mexico and Slovakia.

headings: Risks Related to Adient's Global Business
Unfavorable changes in the condition of the global automotive industry and the condition of individual automakers may adversely affect Adient's results of operations.
Risks associated with joint venture partnerships may adversely affect Adient's business and financial results.
Risks associated with Adient's non-U.S. operations could adversely affect Adient's business, financial condition and results of operations.
Adient's business in China is subject to aggressive competition and is sensitive to economic and market conditions.
Recent changes in U.S. administrative policy, including increases in tariffs and any changes in international trade relations or trade agreements, may have an adverse effect on Adient.
The regulation of Adient's international operations, and any failure of Adient to comply with those regulations, could adversely affect its business, results of operations and reputation.
Increases in the costs and restrictions on the availability of raw materials, energy, commodities, freight, labor and product components could adversely affect Adient's financial performance.
Adient operates in the highly competitive automotive supply industry which requires capital expenditures to support customer launch plans and growth.
Work stoppages, including those at Adient's customers, and similar events could significantly disrupt Adient's business.
Adient may be unable to realize the expected benefits of its restructuring actions, which could adversely affect its profitability and operations.
Negative or unexpected tax consequences could adversely affect Adient's results of operations.
If Adient does not respond appropriately, the evolution of the automotive industry towards autonomous vehicles and mobility on demand services could adversely affect Adient's business.
Adient may incur material losses and costs as a result of warranty and product recall claims and product liability actions that may be brought against Adient.
Any changes in consumer credit availability or cost of borrowing could adversely affect Adient's business.
Global climate change and related emphasis on sustainability matters by various stakeholders could negatively affect Adient's business.
Risks related to Adient's defined benefit retirement plans may adversely impact Adient's results of operations and cash flow.
Legal proceedings in which Adient is, or may be, a party may adversely affect Adient.
A downgrade in the ratings of Adient's debt capital could restrict Adient's ability to access the debt capital markets and increase Adient's interest costs.
Adient's debt obligations could adversely affect Adient's business, profitability and the ability to meet its obligations.
Adient's business success depends on attracting and retaining qualified personnel and the attempt to operate under a hybrid working environment may not be successful.
Adverse developments affecting, or the financial distress of, one or more of Adient's suppliers or other third-party counterparties could adversely affect Adient's financial performance.
The loss of business with respect to, or the lack of commercial success of, a vehicle model for which Adient is a significant supplier could adversely affect Adient's financial performance.
paragraphs: The following discussion of risk factors contains forward-looking statements. These risk factors may be important to understanding other statements in this Form 10-K. The following information should be read in conjunction with Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and the consolidated financial statements and related notes in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Form 10-K.

The business, financial condition and operating results of Adient can be affected by a number of factors, whether currently known or unknown, including but not limited to those described below, any one or more of which could, directly or indirectly, cause Adient's actual financial condition and operating results to vary materially from past, or from anticipated future, financial condition and operating results. Any of these factors, in whole or in part, could materially and adversely affect Adient's business, financial condition, operating results and stock price.

Because of the following factors, as well as other factors affecting Adient's financial condition and operating results, past financial performance should not be considered to be a reliable indicator of future performance, and investors should not use historical trends to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

General economic, credit, capital market and global political conditions could adversely affect Adient's financial performance, Adient's ability to grow or sustain its businesses and Adient's ability to access the capital markets.

Adient competes around the world in various geographic regions and product markets. Global economic conditions, including global demand for new vehicles, new vehicle affordability, supply chain disruptions, inflationary concerns and labor availability, affect Adient's business. As discussed in greater detail below, any future distress in the industries and/or markets where Adient competes could negatively affect Adient's revenues and financial performance in future periods, result in future restructuring charges, and adversely impact Adient's ability to grow or sustain its businesses.

The global automotive industry has continued to experience uncertainties due to changing macroeconomic conditions. Weakening consumer demand, impacted by new vehicle affordability and a high interest rate environment, among other factors, has resulted in lower automotive production volumes. The global adoption of electric vehicles by consumers has also slowed, creating disruptions in production scheduling. More specifically, the EMEA region is faced with overcapacity issues due to lower production volumes and resulting in pricing pressures. The EMEA region is also faced with intensifying competition from Chinese imports and lower exports to China as domestic brands expand in China. The Asia region is also experiencing higher competitive pressures from local OEMs in China who are penetrating the industry with new product offerings. These Chinese OEMs are producing vehicles at lower costs, resulting in pricing pressures on the supply chain base. Further, new relationships need to be developed in order to become the supplier of choice for these new OEMs in China along with careful assessment of which local OEMs are expected to exist and thrive over the long-term due to the competitive pressures. Adient strives to offset the impact of lower production volumes and price reductions through improved operational performance, including commercial negotiations with Adient's customers and vendors and through other operational improvements that Adient can influence, however there is no guarantee that Adient will be able to sufficiently offset the impact of lower production volumes, price reductions, or avoid more significant restructuring actions. The global automotive industry has also experienced significant volatility in the past, and to some extent volatility persists in the current environment, related to supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures, labor shortages, geopolitical uncertainties, high interest rates and foreign currency fluctuations. Although Adient's seating products have not typically been dependent directly on the components causing the supply chain disruptions, Adient has been directly impacted by lower production levels at the OEMs as a direct result of these disruptions. These disruptions have moderated in fiscal 2025, but supply chains remain fragile and, in the past have led to unplanned downtime at Adient's production facilities, often with very little warning, which created operating inefficiencies and limited Adient's ability to adequately mitigate such inefficiencies. The automotive industry has also experienced a period of significant price volatility (generally resulting in an increase in commodities, energy costs, freight costs, labor costs and other input costs), as well as encountering an environment of unfavorable foreign currency exposures and rising interest rates. While some of these input cost increases have moderated in fiscal 2025, other exposures will likely continue into fiscal 2026 and perhaps further into the future. This environment of significant price volatility has resulted in, and may continue to result in, increased costs for Adient that may not be, or may only be partially, offset. Adient also experienced constrained labor availability which has resulted in wage inflationary pressures, both internally and at key vendors. Adient continues to assess any impact labor shortages and wage inflation might have on Adient's ability to perform its obligations. Although Adient has developed and implemented strategies to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions along with the impact of higher input and other costs, these strategies, together with commercial negotiations with Adient's customers and suppliers, typically offset only a portion (less than 100%) of the adverse impact. Adient is a global leader in the automotive seating supply industry and maintains relationships with the largest global automotive original equipment manufacturers, or OEMs. Adient's proprietary technologies extend into virtually every area of automotive seating solutions, including complete seating systems, frames, mechanisms, foam, head restraints, armrests and trim covers. Adient is an independent seat supplier with global scale and the capability to design, develop, engineer, manufacture and deliver complete seat systems and components in every major automotive producing region in the world.

Adient designs, manufactures and markets a full range of seating systems and components for passenger cars, commercial vehicles and light trucks, including vans, pick-up trucks and sport/crossover utility vehicles. Adient operates approximately 200 wholly- and majority-owned manufacturing, assembly or sequencing facilities, with operations in 29 countries. Additionally, Adient has partially-owned affiliates in China, Asia, Europe and North America. Through its global footprint and vertical integration, Adient leverages its capabilities to drive growth in the automotive seating industry.

Adient manages its business on a geographic basis and operates in the following three reportable segments for financial reporting purposes: 1) Americas, which is inclusive of North America and South America; 2) Europe, the Middle East and Africa ("EMEA") and 3) Asia Pacific/China ("Asia").

Adient evaluates the performance of its reportable segments using an adjusted EBITDA metric defined as income (loss) before income taxes and noncontrolling interests, excluding net financing charges, restructuring and impairment costs, restructuring-related costs, net mark-to-market adjustments on pension plans, transaction gains/losses, purchase accounting amortization, depreciation, stock-based compensation and other non-recurring items ("Adjusted EBITDA"). Also, certain corporate-related costs are not allocated to the segments. The reportable segments are consistent with how management views the markets served by Adient and reflect the financial information that is reviewed by its chief operating decision maker. Refer to Note 17, "Segment Information," of the notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information on Adient's reportable segments.

Adient, along with the automotive industry, faces uncertainties surrounding future production volume within the automotive industry. These uncertainties are the result of a combination of factors including weakening consumer demand due in part to vehicle affordability, the direct and indirect impacts resulting from the imposition of U.S. and foreign tariffs, market share loss for foreign/luxury OEMs in the Asia reporting unit combined with modest expected margin declines as Adient continues to win new business with local OEMs in China, intensifying competition from Chinese imports and lower exports to China from EMEA as domestic brands expand in China, overcapacity in the EMEA reporting unit resulting in pricing pressure, continued disruptions caused by slower EV adoption rates, and interruptions from other suppliers due to production downtime and shortages of critical components or raw materials. Adient has also been experiencing increased levels of discussions with taxing authorities and more aggressive negotiations by the tax authorities as part of tax audits and related inquiries, resulting in higher levels of uncertainty on tax assessment outcomes. These factors are expected to continue to exist into fiscal 2026 at varying degrees which will continue to negatively impact Adient's results for the foreseeable future. Refer to the consolidated results of operations and segment analysis discussion below for additional information on the impacts of these items on Adient's results.

Adient conducts its business globally in the automotive industry, which is highly competitive and sensitive to economic, political and social factors in the various regions. During fiscal 2025, global light vehicle production increased 3.0%, driven by improved vehicle sales and stronger export activity in China, partially offset by reduced production volumes in North America and EMEA. The current operating environment varies by region, being impacted by weakening consumer demand due to new vehicle affordability and high interest rates along with slower electric vehicle adoption rates.

paragraphs: Adient plc ("Adient") 為全球汽車座椅供應產業的領導者，在美洲、歐洲及亞洲擁有領導市場地位，並與全球最大的汽車原廠製造商 ("OEMs") 保持長期合作關係。Adient 的專有技術已延伸至汽車座椅解決方案的幾乎所有領域，包括完整的座椅系統、框架、機械結構、泡沫、頭部支撐、扶手及裝飾蓋。Adient 是一家全球座椅供應商，具備設計、開發、工程、製造及交付完整座椅系統與零組件的能力，可在全球主要汽車製造地區進行操作。
Adient 設計、製造及行銷用於乘用車、商用車及輕型卡車（包括貨車、皮卡及休旅車）的完整座椅系統與零組件。Adient 約擁有 200 個全資及多數股權的製造、組裝或排序工廠，業務遍及 29 個國家。此外，Adient 在中國、亞洲、歐洲及北美地區亦有部分股權的子公司。透過其全球佈局與垂直整合，Adient 能夠發揮其能力，推動汽車座椅產業的成長。
Adient 的商業模式聚焦於開發與維護長期客戶關係，使其能與全球領導原廠製造商 (OEMs) 一同成長。Adient 及其工程師與客戶密切合作，協助車輛平台的開發，這使其與 OEM 客戶的關鍵決策者建立緊密聯繫。
全球製造佈局 Adient 是全球汽車座椅產業的領導者。擁有超過 65,000 名員工，在全球 29 個國家約 200 個製造、組裝或排序工廠運作，Adient 能為所有車型類別及主要 OEM 製造並交付汽車座椅。從完整的座椅系統到個別零組件，Adient 的製造能力涵蓋汽車座椅製造的每個環節。整合的內部技能使 Adient 能從研究與設計一路到工程與製造，並每年為數百萬輛車提供產品。

運營效率 Adient 意圖維持高製造利用率並透過持續使用標準化製造流程來提高效率，這是其核心競爭優勢。這些標準化製造流程使 Adient 能提供高品質水準並減少浪費。Adient 透過全球製造佈局與整合供應鏈取得規模優勢。Adient 還透過其整合模組化組裝流程，創造效率並優化存貨、降低運輸及直接人工成本。Adient 培養持續改進的環境，透過分析流程與成本指標識別最佳商業實踐，並將這些實踐在全球製造網路中分享。
為確保適當的服務水準、最小存貨及最佳工廠利用率，Adient 採用銷售與運營規劃 (Sales & Operational Planning, 或 S&OP) 流程。一個執行良好的 S&OP 流程提供兩項戰略優勢：聚焦的客戶服務與準時交貨，這會導致客戶留存及市場佔有率的機會。
投資於科技 Adient 繼續投資於科技與創新，透過在金屬、泡沫、裝飾及完整座椅操作中使用自動化，以及擴展人工智慧 ("AI") 的應用。AI 技術正被追求以減少直接人工成本、提高準確性並確保可重複且可重製的結果。
與領導全球 OEM 的長期客戶關係 Adient 與 OEM 合作開發完整的座椅解決方案，以符合消費者對性能、安全與舒適的期待。Adient 與所有主要全球 OEM 客戶合作，並在許多情況下與這些客戶密切合作，開發整合於整體車輛外觀與結構的座椅解決方案。
透過專屬客戶團隊，Adient 與其全球 OEM 客戶維持緊密關係。這些關係使 Adient 能夠清楚瞭解其客戶需求，使其能符合客戶需求。Adient 的客戶團隊也領導新業務取得流程，確保與 Adient 的產品、製造與製造策略一致。
產品創新與製造領導 Adient 在多年來有強勁的記錄，開發獲勝的產品與製造技術，這已為 Adient 及其客戶創造競爭優勢。管理階層預期會增加創新投資。

Adient 會使用全球核心產品組合，或 CPP，策略用於所有產品應用的零件與設計重複使用。Adient 預期會持續投資其 CPP 以維持並擴大其市場成功，並利用其現有的模組化與可擴充系統及可交換零組件。透過 CPP 策略，Adient 為其客戶提供高品質產品，具市場競爭成本與大量（低重量以提高燃油經濟性），同時符合其性能需求。Adient 繼續使用其 CPP 推進 Adient 的精益製造計畫，透過提供標準、靈活的流程來減少複雜性、存貨與廠房空間。這將導致開發時間、產品成本與投資減少。
全球開發網路 Adient 參與創新與開發汽車座椅業務中的關鍵競爭差異點。在開發流程中，產品的關鍵下游元素會被鎖定，包括材料成本、工廠轉換成本、品質特性與某些技術需求。Adient 使用全球一致的產品開發流程，確保這些元素在開發流程開始時正確，反映 Adient 全球運作的最佳實踐，並符合 Adient 多樣化客戶羣的期望。其產品發佈系統可根據客戶與產品需求進行客製化與擴充。
Adient 的全球工程網路包含十個核心開發中心。這些開發中心使用全球一致的方法來開發座椅產品的流程。透過利用主題技術專家網路，Adient 有效落實最佳實踐並改善產品成本與品質。Adient 的產品開發實踐也包含利用低成本國家開發中心，包括印度、中國、捷克共和國、墨西哥與斯洛伐克。

paragraphs: 除非上下文另有要求，否則提及「Adient plc」或「Adient」均指 Adient plc 及其合併子公司。本處所呈現之資訊係基於管理階層對 Adient 營運成果之觀點。

Adient 在本節及其他部分之年度報告表 10-K 中，已作出若干聲明，這些聲明係基於管理階層對未來資訊之觀點，因此，這些聲明受風險與不確定性所影響。本表 10-K 中除歷史事實之陳述外，其他所有陳述均為「未來展望性陳述」，依 1995 年私人證券訴訟改革法案之定義。在本表 10-K 中，關於 Adient 未來財務狀況、銷售、成本、獲利、現金流或其他營運成果衡量指標、資本支出或債務水準及計畫、目標、展望、指引或目標之陳述均為未來展望性陳述。詞彙如「未來」、「可能」、「將」、「會」、「可以」、「預期」、「意圖」、「估計」、「預期」、「相信」、「應該」、「預測」、「預測」、「計畫」或具有相似意義之詞彙，通常用以識別未來展望性陳述。Adient 警告這些陳述受許多重要風險、不確定性、假設及其他因素影響，部分因素為 Adient 無法控制，這些因素可能導致 Adient 實際結果與該等未來展望性陳述所表達或暗示者有重大差異，包括但不限於：地方與國家經濟、信貸與資本市場條件（包括高利率持續、車輛負擔能力及波動匯率）對全球經濟之影響、EMEA 與亞洲地區來自中國 OEM 之競爭壓力增加、美國行政政策對貿易協議、關稅及其他國際貿易關係之不確定性、汽車車輛生產量、組合與排程，以及對特定汽車製造商（特別是中國市場之新進廠商）之集中風險、車輛市場佔有率之變動、車輛段別或離開 Adient 有重大內容之車輛、消費者需求之變動、與 Adient 之合資企業相關之風險、波動能源市場、Adient 顧客對增加投入成本之回復能力與時間、原材料與零組件之可得性（包括 Adient 顧客製造車輛所需之零組件）、與保固與產品回購及產品責任暴露相關之風險、地緣政治不確定性如烏克蘭與中東衝突及其對區域與全球經濟之影響、對供應鏈與車輛生產之額外壓力、Adient 有效啟動新業務之能力與預期獲利水準、Adient 成功識別合適之有機投資與/或收購機會並整合這些投資與/或收購之能力、罷工（包括因罷工、供應鏈中斷等事件）、因勞動力短缺與新勞資談判所致之工資通貨膨脹壓力、Adient 執行其重整計畫並達成預期效益之能力、Adient 依債務償還要求與未來融資條款之能力、全球稅制改革法案之影響、稅務當局更積極立場之影響、遞延稅資產價值之潛在調整、全球氣候變遷及各相關利害關係人對永續議題之強調，以及 Adient 達成其永續相關目標之能力、合約取消或變更，以及 Adient 識別、招募與留住關鍵領導階層之能力。導致差異的因素包括但不限於，如 Part 1, Item 1A 所討論之風險因素，已於本表 10-K 中引用。本處所呈現之資訊係基於 Adient 之財務曆程。除非另有說明，提及特定年份、季度、月份或期間均指 Adient 財務年度結算於 9 月，以及該財務年度相關之季度、月份及期間。本表 10-K 所包含之未來展望性陳述係於本報告日作出，除非另有說明，且除非法律要求，Adient 假設無義務，亦否認任何義務，更新此等陳述以反映本表 10-K 日期後發生之事件或情況。
Adient 為全球汽車座椅供應產業之領導者，並與全球最大之汽車原廠製造商（OEMs）維持關係。Adient 之專利技術已延伸至汽車座椅解決方案之幾乎所有領域，包括完整座椅系統、框架、機械結構、泡沫、頭部支撐、扶手與裝飾蓋。Adient 為獨立座椅供應商，具備全球規模與能力，可設計、開發、工程、製造與交付完整座椅系統與零組件，於全球主要汽車製造地區。
Adient 設計、製造與行銷用於乘客車、商用車與輕型卡車（包括貨車、皮卡與休旅車）之完整座椅系統與零組件。Adient 約經營 200 個全資與多數持股之製造、組裝或排序工廠，於 29 個國家有業務。此外，Adient 在中國、亞洲、歐洲與北美有部分持股之附屬公司。透過其全球據點與垂直整合，Adient 藉助其能力以推動汽車座椅產業之成長。
Adient 依地理區域管理其業務，並於財務報導目的下經營以下三個應報告分部：1) 美洲（包括北美洲與南美洲）；2) 歐洲、中東與非洲（"EMEA"）；3) 亞太/中國（"亞洲"）。

Adient 依調整後之 EBITDA 指標評估其應報告分部之表現，此指標定義為收入（虧損）扣除所得稅與非控制權益，排除淨融資費用、重整與減損成本、重整相關成本、淨市價調整（退休金計畫）、交易損益、購併會計折舊、折舊、股票基於報酬支出及其他非經常性項目（"調整後 EBITDA"）。此外，某些公司相關成本未分配至分部。應報告分部與管理階層視為 Adient 所服務市場之方式一致，並反映其首席營運決策者所審閱之財務資訊。請參閱附註 17，"分部資訊"，於合併財務報表附註中以取得更多關於 Adient 應報告分部之資訊。

Adient 與汽車產業一樣，面臨未來生產量之不確定性。這些不確定性係因多種因素所致，包括因車輛負擔能力而導致之消費者需求減弱、美國與外國關稅施加之直接與間接影響、亞洲報告單位中外資/豪華 OEM 之市場佔有率流失，以及因 Adient 繼續與中國本地 OEM 獲得新業務，導致預期邊際率下降，同時中國市場中中國進口競爭加劇，以及 EMEA 報告單位對中國出口減少，因本地品牌在中國擴張，EMEA 報告單位過度生產導致價格壓力，持續因電動車採用率較慢所致之幹擾，以及因生產停機與關鍵零組件或原材料短缺所致之供應商中斷。Adient 亦經歷與稅務當局之討論增加，以及稅務當局在稅務稽核與相關查詢中更積極之談判，導致稅務評估結果之不確定性提高。這些因素預期將持續至財務 2026 年，程度不一，將持續對 Adient 之結果產生負面影響。請參閱下文合併營運成果與分部分析討論，以取得更多關於這些項目對 Adient 結果影響之資訊。
Adient 在全球汽車產業中經營業務，該產業高度競爭，且對各區域之經濟、政治與社會因素敏感。在財務 2025 年，全球輕型車輛生產量增加 3.0%，因中國之車輛銷售改善與出口活動強化，部分抵銷北美洲與 EMEA 之生產量減少。目前營運環境因地區而異，受新車輛負擔能力與高利率導致之消費者需求減弱及電動車採用率較慢影響。

headings: 與 Adient 全球業務相關的風險
全球汽車產業及個別汽車製造商營運狀況惡化，可能對 Adient 的營運成果產生負面影響。
與合資企業合作夥伴相關的風險可能對 Adient 的業務與財務結果產生負面影響。
與 Adient 非美國運營相關的風險可能對 Adient 的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
Adient 在中國的業務面臨激烈競爭，且對經濟與市場狀況變化較為敏感。
美國行政政策近期的變動，包括關稅的提高以及國際貿易關係或貿易協議的任何變更，可能對 Adient 產生不利影響。
Adient 的國際業務受到規範，且 Adient 若未能遵守這些規範，可能會對其業務、營運結果及聲譽產生不利影響。
與 Adient 營運相關的風險
原材料、能源、商品、運輸、勞動力及產品零組件的成本增加及取得限制，可能對 Adient 的財務表現產生不利影響。
Adient 營運於高度競爭的汽車供應鏈產業，此產業需要資本支出以支持客戶的發佈計畫及成長。
工會罷工，包括 Adient 的客戶所發生的罷工，及其他類似事件，可能對 Adient 的業務造成顯著幹擾。
Adient 可能無法實現其重整行動預期的效益，這可能會對其獲利能力及營運產生不利影響。
負面或意外的稅務後果可能會對 Adient 的營運結果產生不利影響。
若 Adient 未能適當回應，汽車產業朝向自動駕駛車輛及隨需應變交通服務的演進，可能會對 Adient 的業務產生不利影響。
Adient 可能因保証及產品回購聲請及產品責任訴訟而產生重大損失及成本。
消費者信貸可得性或借款成本的變動可能會對 Adient 的業務產生不利影響。
全球氣候變遷及各相關利害關係人對永續議題的重視，可能會對 Adient 的業務產生負面影響。
與 Adient 之定義受益退休計畫相關之風險可能對 Adient 之營運成果及現金流產生負面影響。
Adient 參與之法律程序可能對 Adient 產生負面影響。
Adient 之債務資本評級 downgrade 可能限制 Adient 進入債務資本市場之能力，並提高 Adient 之利息成本。
Adient 之債務義務可能對 Adient 之業務、獲利能力及履行其義務之能力產生負面影響。
Adient 之業務成功取決於吸引及留住合格人員，且試圖在混合式工作環境下運作可能無法成功。
影響 Adient 之一或多個供應商或其他第三方對手之不利發展，或其財務困境，可能對 Adient 之財務表現產生負面影響。

paragraphs: 下列風險因素的討論包含前瞻性陳述。這些風險因素可能對理解本 Form 10-K 其他陳述非常重要。下列資訊應與本 Form 10-K 第二部分，第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」以及第二部分，第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」所載之合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。
Adient 的業務、財務狀況與營運成果可能受多種因素影響，無論是否已知或未知，包括但不限於下列所描述的因素，任何一項或數項因素，可能直接或間接導致 Adient 實際財務狀況與營運成果與過去或預期未來財務狀況與營運成果有重大差異。這些因素，全部或部分，可能對 Adient 的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與股票價格造成重大且不利的影響。
由於下列因素，以及影響 Adient 財務狀況與營運成果的其他因素，過去財務表現不應視為未來表現的可靠指標，投資人亦不應以歷史趨勢預測未來期間的結果或趨勢。
總體經濟、信貸、資本市場及全球政治條件可能對 Adient 的財務表現、Adient 維持或擴張其業務的能力，以及 Adient 接入資本市場的能力造成不利影響。
Adient 在世界各地不同地理區域與產品市場進行競爭。全球經濟條件，包括新車需求、新車負擔能力、供應鏈中斷、通貨膨脹擔憂與勞動力可得性，影響 Adient 的業務。如後文更詳細討論，Adient 競爭產業與/或市場未來可能出現的困難，可能對 Adient 未來期間的收入與財務表現造成負面影響，導致未來重整費用，並對 Adient 維持或擴張其業務的能力造成不利影響。

全球汽車產業持續因變動的總體經濟條件而面臨不確定性。消費者需求因新車負擔能力與高利率環境等因素而減弱，導致汽車生產量降低。消費者對電動車的全球採用也減緩，造成生產排程的中斷。更明確地，EMEA 區域因生產量降低而面臨過度生產能力問題，導致價格壓力。EMEA 區域也因中國進口競爭加劇與對中國出口減少而面臨挑戰，因國內品牌在中國擴張。亞洲區域也因中國本地 OEM 品牌進佔產業而面臨更高競爭壓力，這些中國 OEM 品牌以較低成本生產車輛，導致供應鏈基礎的價格壓力。此外，需建立新關係以成為這些中國 OEM 品牌的首選供應商，並謹慎評估哪些本地 OEM 品牌預期能在長遠內存續與成長，因競爭壓力所致。Adient 嘗試透過改善營運表現，包括與 Adient 客戶與供應商的商業談判，以及 Adient 可影響的其他營運改善措施，來抵消生產量降低與價格減幅的影響，但 Adient 無法保證能足夠抵消生產量降低、價格減幅，或避免更嚴重的重整措施。全球汽車產業也經歷過顯著的波動，目前環境中，部分波動仍持續存在，與供應鏈中斷、通貨膨脹壓力、勞動力短缺、地緣政治不確定性、高利率與外匯波動有關。雖然 Adient 的座椅產品通常不直接依賴造成供應鏈中斷的零組件，但 Adient 因 OEM 生產量降低而直接受到影響，這是這些中斷的結果。這些中斷在財務 2025 年已有所緩和，但供應鏈仍處於脆弱狀態，過去曾導致 Adient 生產設施出現未預期的停機，通常事先幾乎沒有警告，造成營運低效率，並限制 Adient 足夠緩解這些低效率的能力。汽車產業也經歷了一段顯著的價格波動期（通常導致原材料、能源成本、運輸費用、勞動成本及其他投入成本增加），以及面臨不利的外匯 exposures 環境與利率上升。雖然部分投入成本增加在財務 2025 年已有所緩和，但其他 exposures 可能會持續至財務 2026 年，甚至更長時間。這種顯著的價格波動環境已導致，且可能繼續導致 Adient 成本增加，這些成本可能無法完全抵銷。Adient 也經歷了勞動力可得性受限，導致內部與關鍵供應商的工資通貨膨脹壓力。Adient 繼續評估勞動力短缺與工資通脹對 Adient 履行其義務能力的影響。雖然 Adient 已發展並實施策略以緩解供應鏈中斷以及投入成本及其他成本的影響，這些策略，加上與 Adient 客戶與供應商的商業談判，通常只能抵銷部分（少於 100%）的負面影響。此外，Adient 的營運模式需要在
